standard_prerequisites.name: Second-order arithmetic, countable topped models and the principle WF(alpha)
standard_prerequisites.statement: RCA_0 is the usual base theory of reverse mathematics; a countable model M = (M,S) is topped by a set Y in S when every set of the model is computable from Y; WF(alpha) states that the ordinal alpha is well founded, and an M-infinite decreasing sequence of ordinals below a bound is a sequence indexed by the model's own natural numbers.
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the meaning of the hypothesis of the counted lemma and of the conclusion that a Turing functional is an M-infinite decreasing sequence below the natural product bound.

standard_prerequisites.name: Turing functionals, indices and their computable manipulation
standard_prerequisites.statement: Turing functionals with oracle X are written as Phi-sub-e to the X, an index of a functional can be found computably from its parameters, and functionals may be twisted so that the value at a given input depends only on an initial segment of the oracle.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof begins by twisting the functionals so that convergence forces the three normalisation properties, and the statement itself promises that an index of the blocking functional can be found computably in k.

standard_prerequisites.name: Natural (Hessenberg) sum and product below epsilon-zero
standard_prerequisites.statement: For ordinals below epsilon-zero written in Cantor normal form with a common family of exponents, the natural sum adds the coefficients exponent by exponent, the natural product alpha times k is the natural sum of k copies of alpha, and the natural sum is strictly increasing in each argument.
standard_prerequisites.use: The blocking functional outputs the natural sum of the k last values, and the strict decrease of that sum is what makes the output an M-infinite descending sequence below the natural product bound.

core_obligations: Normalise the given Turing functionals: verify that by twisting them one may assume that for every e and n in the model, if Phi-sub-e to the sigma converges at n then n is smaller than the length of sigma, the functional converges at every smaller input, and its values at 0 up to n form a strictly decreasing sequence of ordinals below beta (source lines 434-439).

Define alpha(sigma,e) as the value of Phi-sub-e to the sigma at the largest input below the length of sigma where it converges, and beta when there is no such input, and record that alpha(sigma-prime,e) is at most alpha(sigma,e) whenever sigma-prime extends sigma (source line 441).

Build the Turing functional Gamma-sub-k: on input n it searches for x larger than the length of the previous witness sigma-sub-(n-1) and for sigma-sub-n extending the oracle X such that Phi-sub-e to the sigma-sub-n converges at x for some e below k, and, when it finds them, outputs the natural sum of alpha at e = 0 up to e = k-1 (source lines 443-444).
Show the output is an ordinal below the natural product beta times k, using the normalisation property (3) of the first step (source line 444).

Assume the oracle X is such that the model built from X satisfies RCA_0 and that Phi-sub-e to the X is total for some e below k; conclude from the induction scheme for Sigma-0-1 formulas available in the model that Gamma-sub-k to the X is total (source lines 446-447).

Prove Gamma-sub-k to the X is strictly decreasing: the search condition x larger than the length of sigma-sub-(n-1) together with normalisation properties (1), (2) and (3) forces alpha at the successor stage to be strictly smaller than alpha at the previous stage, so Gamma-sub-k to the X is an M-infinite decreasing sequence of ordinals below the natural product (source lines 448-449).

proof_roadmap.step: Twist the functionals to normalise convergence, and define the ordinal-valued measurement alpha(sigma,e) with its monotonicity in sigma.
Define the blocking functional Gamma-sub-k by searching for a new converging value beyond the previous witness length and outputting the natural sum of the k measurements, bounded below beta times k.
Use totality of one Phi-sub-e to the X together with the model's Sigma-0-1 induction to make Gamma-sub-k total, and the normalisation properties to make it strictly decreasing.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the lemma labelled lem:shore-blocking-wf at source lines 426-431: from any failure of well-foundedness below an ordinal beta witnessed by one of finitely many Turing functionals, it builds a single Turing functional Gamma-sub-k whose output is an M-infinite decreasing sequence below the natural product beta times k, with an index computable in k. The work is concentrated in the second half of the proof: the functionals are first twisted so that convergence at an input forces convergence at every smaller input and a strictly decreasing run of values below beta (source lines 434-439), and only then can the measurement alpha(sigma,e) be defined as the last convergent value and proved monotone in the oracle segment (source line 441). The blocking functional searches beyond the length of the previously found segment rather than beyond the previous input, which is what makes the newly found value strictly smaller than the old one (source lines 443-444 and 448-449); the natural sum of the k measurements is what converts k separate partial failures into one sequence, and the natural product bound beta times k is exactly what the companion lemma lem:wf-product needs. Totality of the blocking functional is not free either: it comes from totality of a single Phi-sub-e to the X plus the induction scheme for Sigma-0-1 formulas available in the model (source lines 446-447).
